findings.desc: The new quantum_claim_benchmark and quantum_claim_report commands are added to COMMAND_POLICIES but are not classified in PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS. This breaks the lifecycle registry/process-fact consistency contract: npm run test:lifecycle-registry-contract fails with process-fact-lifecycle divergences for both commands. Add L0 process-fact lifecycle entries matching their read-only diagnostic policy before merge.

B-3779 M4 claims the implemented benchmark covers the planned/source-of-truth B1-B15 adversarial injections, but the runtime corpus is different. plan.md lines 24-39 and the Quantum source doc lines 258-277 define B1-B15 as domain scenarios such as Hamiltonian/potential/boundary/timestep changes, normalization/residual/invariant failures, units mismatch, random seed missing, and manually edited table/plot. packages/main/src/core/claim-admissibility/quantum.ts lines 1445-1460 instead implements B1-B15 as stale/missing Q5 receipt, core field/output/verifier/duplicate/schema/unknown-claim failures, and packages/main/src/tasks/quantum-claim-benchmark-smoke.ts lines 47-63 asserts that different corpus. As a result the benchmark can report PASS without exercising the documented/planned B1-B15 cases. Align the runtime/tests to the documented B1-B15 corpus or explicitly revise the docs/plan/checklist promise so the local diagnostic M4 claim is bounded to the evaluator-failure corpus actually implemented; keep diagnosticOnly/gateEvidence=false and no generic framework/lifecycle/Authority/production/scientific claims.
findings.resolvedReason: Verified fixed by lattice-review-concept in review run B-3779:RR-009.
